I am 61 years old and have farmed these 6.5 mu in Quzhou for 43 years. I know my soil, my well, and the local weather. With only 6.5 mu and some family working off-farm, I cannot waste labor or money on fancy experiments. My foundation is 5 mu of wheat-maize rotation — that is my food security and my stable income. The winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. I will top-dress nitrogen at green-up and irrigate twice more before early June harvest: once at jointing and once at grain filling. I use an improved wheat seed that has done well here for years. After wheat harvest, there is no time to waste for summer maize — the season is short. I will rotary till the same day and plant hybrid maize seed immediately. I will side-dress nitrogen at the big trumpet stage, irrigate two or three times depending on rainfall, and spray for weeds and corn borer.

The remaining 1.5 mu I will plant with hybrid chili this spring. Chili is my cash crop — it brings more money per mu than grain — but it needs more care. I will apply more phosphorus and potassium because fruiting crops need them, and with my well I can irrigate every 10 to 15 days through dry spells, about six times total. I will spray pesticides five times because aphids, thrips, and wilt always come. I keep chili to only 1.5 mu because when picking starts in summer, it is daily work, and with some family away I do not have enough hands to manage more. I do not do no-tillage — I have tried it and the weeds became unmanageable. I ploughed for wheat last fall, I will rotary till for maize after wheat harvest, and I will rotary till for chili now. My fertilizer rates are based on watching what actually puts money in my pocket, not what the seed salesman claims. If the weather cooperates, I expect about 500 kg/mu of wheat, 550 kg/mu of maize, and around 2,000 kg/mu of fresh chili.
